title: Playing for Pizza
subtitle: A Novel
author: John Grisham
bibliographyNote: The US publisher records the hardcover on sale September 24, 2007; the Library of Congress bibliography independently records the novel in 2007. Use the year on the public page to avoid confusing regional publication dates.
deck: A second season. A different measure of success.
intro: Rick Dockery's NFL career has collapsed. The next team willing to take a chance on him is in Parma, Italy, where a familiar game comes with an unfamiliar language and a new way of living. Grisham turns the displaced quarterback's arrival into a warm, comic invitation to reconsider what makes a life worth playing for.
sportNote: The sport is American football: quarterbacks, helmets, and touchdowns. The setting is Parma, Italy.

context.title: Grisham away from the courtroom
context.text: This standalone sports novel offers another entrance to Grisham: a player abroad, a team to understand, and a place to discover.

context.title: A novel, not a travel itinerary
context.text: Read Parma through Rick's initially limited viewpoint. Let the meals, conversations, and games raise questions about how a visitor learns to belong.

pathways.title: Read for the game
pathways.text: Follow the difference between a player's reputation and what a team needs from him. Keep a note of the moments when the scale of the game changes his expectations.

pathways.title: Read for the place
pathways.text: Pay attention to what Rick understands quickly and what asks him to slow down. Notice the daily rituals through which a new city becomes legible.

pathways.title: Read together
pathways.text: Start with one spoiler-light question: what do we carry with us when our old definition of success stops working? Open the discussion guide only after reading.

deeper.label: After reading: themes and discussion
deeper.spoilerNotice: Optional discussion for readers who have finished the novel. Open deliberately; answers may involve later events and the ending.

themes.title: Success at another scale
themes.text: Consider whether status, useful work, and satisfaction move together or pull apart.

themes.title: Belonging as practice
themes.text: Look at the part played by attention, hospitality, and repeated shared activities.

themes.title: Sport as pleasure and obligation
themes.text: Ask what remains when the rewards attached to a sport change.

discussion: Where does Rick's definition of success begin to change? Which scene makes that change convincing to you?
How do the teammates' reasons for playing challenge Rick's assumptions about the game?
Choose a meal or a conversation. What does the scene accomplish that a game scene could not?
When does the comedy invite us to sympathize with Rick, and when does it ask us to question him?
How does the novel distinguish being welcomed from making the effort to belong?
Does the ending resolve Rick's problem, redefine it, or leave a useful tension? Support your answer with a scene.
